issue.title: Memory-read reports print re-resolved current content under ## Output, unlabeled, instead of the recorded read

task_type_fields.impact: The Agents-tab MAIN Context MEMORY lane hints materialize these reports today. A user who asks "what did this agent read?" gets current content presented as what was read, unlabeled. It can come from another agent's checkout of the same reused workspace. Fix options: render `## Output` from the recorded blob OIDs when they are available (`included_blob_oids` / `blob_oid`). Otherwise label the section "Re-resolved now (not the recorded output)", or show only the recorded metadata. Found while consolidating `research:202610/agent_memory_deck_placement/agent_memory_deck_placement__final.md` (§2.4); any future MEMORY deck must not reuse this path as historical content.
task_type_fields.repro:
1. `src/sase/memory/memory_read_report.py::_build_memory_read_report` calls `_resolve_report_view(event, selectors)`, which runs `resolve_memory_selector_batch(...)` with `project_root=Path(event.cwd)` and the live `home_root`. The source is whatever exists at that path *now*.
2. `event.cwd` is the reading agent's ephemeral `sase_<N>` workspace, for example `/home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_13`. Later agents reuse that workspace at other commits, or it no longer exists.
3. The report prints that re-resolved text under a plain `## Output` heading. It has no label saying the text is current rather than recorded. Meanwhile `## Versions read` (`_versions_read_lines`) lists the recorded `blob:<oid>` values, which may not match the printed text.
4. Repro: pick any `memory_reads.jsonl` event older than a few days whose note has since changed, for example a `tui.md` or `decisions:*` read. Open its MEMORY-lane hint in the Agents tab (or call `write_memory_read_report`). Compare `## Output` with `git cat-file -p <recorded blob>`. The output shows today's checkout of that workspace, not the bytes the agent read.

issue.creation_reason: Filed during memory-deck research consolidation: the memory-read report path silently presents current, possibly foreign, workspace content as what an agent read, which misleads the existing MAIN lane hints and any future MEMORY deck.
